text:
OpsBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Unusual S3 GET pattern detected for bucket redwood-prod-logs at 03:21 UTC — 214 GETs across 3 client IPs in 120s. Triggered rule: S3-Access-Spike. PagerDuty: sec-oncall triggered.
Maya: I'm taking sec-oncall. Paging @Sam (infra-oncall) and @Lucas (platform-eng) — joining.
Sam: on it. pulling logs now.
Lucas: I'll start a credential sweep and check service keys for svc-ingest and svc-logs.
Maya: quick summary from the alert: path pattern /ingest/*, many objects read, user-agent "curl/7.86" and "python-requests/2.31". Suspect read started 03:19:53 UTC.
Sam: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T03:19:54Z GET s3://redwood-prod-logs/ingest/2026/03/15/part-0001.log 200 - 18.197.32.11 UA=curl/7.86
2026-03-15T03:19:55Z GET s3://redwood-prod-logs/ingest/2026/03/15/part-0002.log 200 - 34.210.111.5 UA=python-requests/2.31
```
Maya: were those IPs internal or from cloud providers? Sam: mixed — two AWS IPs and one GCP. All external.
Lucas: I'm checking IAM logs for STS assume and AccessKeyId usage. Early indicator: AccessKeyId AKIAEXAMPLE used by svc-ingest-role at 03:19:52.
Maya: ok immediate mitigation plan:
- rotate service keys for svc-ingest and svc-logs (Lucas)
- revoke active STS tokens and sessions for those roles (Lucas)
- add temporary deny on bucket read from public network except our NATs (Sam)
- block the three IPs at WAF and firewall (Sam)
- run a quick content scan for sensitive PII in the accessed objects (Anita)
- prepare customer impact blurb if needed (Jonah)
Sam: WAF rule created and applied to front door; IPs blocked: 18.197.32.11, 34.210.111.5, 52.87.10.9. (deployed)
Lucas: rotating keys now. command:
```
aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLE --status Inactive --user-name svc-ingest
# create new key and update secret manager
```
Lucas: created new keys, updated Secrets Manager, triggered rolling restart for ingest workers to pick up new creds. Invalidated previous AccessKeyId across all regions.
Maya: @Anita any initial findings from content scan? severity note: possible leak of debug logs that may include client IPs and request IDs, no auth tokens visible so far.
Anita: running grep/heuristics over the objects read. Early: ~8 files contained internal request URIs and partial stack traces; nothing looks like clear API keys or full SSNs. marking as "sensitive" pending manual review.
Jonah: drafting customer-facing note: "We detected unauthorized reads from our logs bucket. We rotated keys and blocked access; no evidence of customer data exfiltration. We're conducting a full review and will notify if findings change." Will share draft in #customer-notifications.
Maya: good. tagging incident severity = P2 -> P1? I'm moving to HIGH until we finish review. Creating INC-2776543210 in tracker.
PagerDuty: sec-oncall acknowledged and escalated to security-lead.
Sam: S3 bucket policy tightened to deny GetObject unless source VPC endpoints or specific NAT IP ranges. Command used:
```
aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket redwood-prod-logs --policy file://deny-external-get.json
```
Lucas: STS token revoke complete; all active sessions for svc-ingest invalidated.
Anita: finished quick content triage: marking 8 files for deeper manual review, ran them through scrubbing rules. No customer PII found in those eight, but one file contains full internal hostnames and partial UUIDs.
Maya: added legal and compliance to the loop. @Anita please export the 8 files to secure-forensics for deeper scan.
Anita: done — export path s3://redwood-forensics/2776543210/
Jonah: CS notified via private thread; asked to prepare inbox template and one-off outreach if we need it. ETA 90m for draft.
Maya: timeline update — keys rotated and WAF blocks live within 7 minutes of alert. No further GET spikes after 03:28 UTC. Access patterns look contained.
Sam: also deployed CloudTrail insights query to find any other buckets accessed by same AccessKeyId.
Lucas: found no additional suspicious uses post-rotation. AccessKeyId AKIAEXAMPLE shows activity only in that 2m window.
Maya: next steps: - full forensics scan of all objects accessed - confirm no log shipping to third-party indexes - create postmortem - review credential rotation tooling to make it 1-click.
Anita: uploading notes and indicators to the incident ticket.
Maya: leaving a short handoff — I'm headed offline in 30m. @Lucas please take the next on-call lead once I'm off. If anything else, page sec-oncall.
Lucas: taking lead. I'll keep monitoring for 4 hours and coordinate with forensics.
PagerDuty: incident status changed to "monitoring". Caller cleared.
Maya: thanks team. closing active coordination in this thread, will update the ticket with links and timeline. :white_check_mark:
